modifications: Add an offline standalone Bloodhound Parquet converter over the public standalone reader, with deterministic public-ID projection, latest observed ticker labels and atomic single-file publication.

Preserve all-adjusted OHLC and raw close/volume; infer a separate provider split factor jointly across all eight views using full-history constant split regimes and evidence-bounded exact rational preference under explicit numerical assumptions, without external data, price smoothing or corporate-action certification.

Embed full public-ID mappings, source generations, numerical assumptions and explicit partial-export outcomes in the Parquet footer; reject invalid output and changed inputs without publishing a partial file by default.

Replace --allow-partial with --include-all-passed: attempt all selected public-ID histories under unchanged conversion checks and publish only complete passing identities; snapshot changes and writer failures still abort.

Keep rejection diagnostics and counts on stderr only. Remove omission records, selected counts and partial status from the Parquet footer and stdout; retain identity mappings and group provenance only for identities with published rows.
Use a bounded generation-keyed reader RAM cache, defaulting to 2048 MiB with --cache-mib 0 as an uncached control; create no persistent cache or source copies.

Use the public reader's lightweight locked generation check at final publication instead of reconstructing assignment evidence; preserve eight-view calculations, acceptance checks, schema, identity mapping and output ordering.

Permit an explicitly selected reader RAM cache up to 6144 MiB for an 8 GiB process allowance, retaining the 2048 MiB default and headroom for active histories and the writer; numeric conversion and publication behavior are unchanged.

Stream completed groups in deterministic source-locator order, sorting IDs within each group, instead of pre-reading the universe and revisiting groups in global-ID order; emit actual processed-locator progress and retain only compact tokens for final freshness checks.

Enforce global ID collision and generation gates before atomic publication, discarding staged output on any collision or moving snapshot; retain whole-ID acceptance and stderr-only rejection diagnostics.

Reuse exact equal-view price intervals within each session and reuse already verified rational-factor witnesses when collecting statistics; numerical formulas, all view constraints and conversion acceptance remain unchanged.

Consume the public reader's exact uncontested-history, path, timestamp and cache-accounting optimizations, and compile fixed projection inequalities once with unchanged operation order; retain all column values, factor reports and whole-ID acceptance checks.
Print the in-memory cache/read ledger to stderr after successful publication; keep it out of the Parquet, stdout summary and disk sidecars.

Retain accepted Arrow output in RAM and serialize it in one Parquet write after acquisition; pack row groups across IDs without changing row order, values, mappings, factor checks or whole-ID acceptance.

Share an explicit memory allowance between retained output and dynamically limited decoded-data caches with reserved working headroom; memory exhaustion aborts the entire export without omissions or disk spill.
Defer all output-file creation until collection succeeds, then retain post-serialization freshness checks and atomic publication; progress and memory diagnostics remain stderr-only.
